newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes release of Chinese dissident.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes release of Chinese dissident.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it welcomed reports that Chinese dissident Chen Ziming had been released from jail to seek medical treatment -- provided he did not have to return to prison afterwards.
"If in fact he has been released and will not be returned to jail, we welcome his release on medical parole," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

Chen, said to be suffering from cancer and other ailments, was serving 13 years for his role in 1989 pro-democracy protests on Beijing's Tiananmen Square. His mother said it was unclear how long he would be permitted to remain at liberty.

"We felt all along, regardless of his medical condition, that he was being held unjustly, as are other political prisoners, political dissidents. They ought all to be released," Burns told a news briefing.

"But particularly in this case, given the humanitarian concerns here, the fact that he is ill, we are pleased by the fact that he apparently has been released and we hope that he will not be returned to any form of incarceration."
